$comment: Runtime configuration for the discovery pipeline. Values here are safe to publish — no secrets. Secrets come only from the environment (TWITTERAPI_IO_KEY, GEMINI_API_KEY).

ingestion.$lookbackComment: Deliberately > 24h. The overlap is harmless because deduplication is keyed on the source-native tweet id, and it stops results falling through the gap at a run boundary.
ingestion.$storeTweetTextComment: Full text is fetched and used for extraction, then reduced to a 160-char excerpt once the observation is resolved (see extraction.redact_resolved). The complete text lives only in data/automation/raw/, which rawRetention prunes. Set false to avoid persisting text even for the run.
ingestion.$pacingComment: TwitterAPI.io returns 429 on rapid bursts (measured: ~40% of 37 back-to-back calls). Requests are paced, not just retried.

rawRetention.$comment: Raw per-day files older than this are pruned by the ingest job. Full API payloads are never committed — they go to a short-retention Actions artifact when debugging.

extraction.$pacingComment: Gemini returns 429 under sustained load: the first real end-to-end run failed 32 of 50 extractions this way, burning 121 calls. The client now paces at this interval and doubles it for subsequent calls on each 429, easing back after successes.

policy.$corroborationComment: A social-media observation with no external identifier (arXiv / DOI / OEIS / Erdős number / Lean or GitHub artifact) may not become a candidate on its own; it goes to the review queue instead. See ARCHITECTURE_ASSESSMENT.md §2.1.

schedule.$comment: Controls the daily run. dryRunOnSchedule starts TRUE deliberately: the first days should observe and report without committing, so the telemetry and review queue can be read before anything is written. Flip to false when the numbers look right — it is a config change, not a code change.
schedule.$cronComment: GitHub Actions cron is UTC-only — there is no timezone field. 04:20 UTC is 07:20 in Bucharest during EEST (summer) and 06:20 during EET (winter); the one-hour drift across DST is documented rather than solved. Off-the-hour because GitHub delays on-the-hour schedules under load.
